title: How is the experience of using Codex for Godot development right now?
author: GouSanSi
selftext:
I'm thinking about starting a new project and would like to know what the current experience is like using Codex to assist with Godot development.

I've been using Codex with Unity, and overall the experience has been pretty good. However, due to some of Unity's quirks and workflow issues, I'm considering moving to Godot.

From some comments I've seen, it seems that AI-assisted development with Godot has not been great in the past, especially compared to Unity. I'm not sure if that is still the case now.

For people currently using Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or similar AI tools with Godot:

How is the experience today?

Is Godot's project structure, GDScript, scene system, and debugging workflow friendly enough for AI-assisted development?

Are there any recommended setups, MCP tools, plugins, or workflows that make Codex work better with Godot?

I'm especially interested in hearing from people who have used both Unity and Godot with AI coding tools.

comments.author: rvgalitein
comments.body: Godot is improving with AI, but it still lags Unity mainly because of ecosystem surface area. Unity has more training data and more consistent patterns, so models behave more predictably. With Godot, you usually get better results when you constrain scope and keep scripts small rather than asking for larger system-level changes.

Full disclosure, I made it. But it’s free and super powerful.  Here’s a UI I made with it in a couple hours. 

https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/s/nGG8dhMGco

replies.author: GouSanSi
replies.body:
That’s really exciting — I’ll definitely give it a try.

I’ve also been using Unity MCP with Unity, and it’s been a great tool. But lately, it feels like the trend is shifting more toward CLI-based workflows. I also tried a project called UnityCliLoop, and if the goal is mainly to let an AI compile, run tests, debug errors, and iterate, the CLI approach really does feel more convenient. It avoids the extra MCP connection layer and keeps the feedback loop simpler.

That said, I don’t think MCP is going away. My impression is that MCP is better when you need richer editor/engine context or deeper integration with Unity, while CLI tools are better for fast, repeatable build-test-debug loops.

How do you see the relationship between CLI-based workflows and MCP going forward?

replies.author: d-czar
replies.body:
Hey! There was a good blog post on CLI/MCP from Anthropic last week: [https://claude.com/blog/building-agents-that-reach-production-systems-with-mcp](https://claude.com/blog/building-agents-that-reach-production-systems-with-mcp)

It basically agrees that CLI is best for local, MCP is better for remote.  

MCP for Unity actually has both MCP and CLI, and I'll add CLI to Godot AI soon too -- I wanted to get MCP and the UX of using/installing/updating the Godot AI plugin really solid first.  I think it's there now.  

So yeah, that's part of why I didn't put MCP in the name -- I want it to to be able to offer the best tools for the job! Let me know if you get a chance to try it, and thanks for the great post!

replies.author: d-czar
replies.body:
That looks really cool. I was a little confused because it seemed like the audio / voiceover was for something else, not the game demo? Either way, very nice work for a couple weeks. Would love to know more about the project. The vfx are cool.

The question of what Godot AI would give you is definitely easier explained by "just try it and you'll see."  But the short version is, it gives your agent a bunch of carefully built and curated  reusable tools for many common engine features -- not just node and scene search and editing but sophisticated screenshotting in game/scene view for editor feedback, UI design tools, automatic test suite running and feedback.  So the models don't have to keep reinventing the wheel by writing custom API tools on the fly.  And there's a community feedback element where people say, hey can you add or improve this tool, so we kind of 'wrap' the most-wanted and useful tools people want.  Give it a try and see what you think -- it takes 2 minutes to install and set up.  Love to hear if you agree it's worthwhile.

comments.author: WildLynxGames
comments.body:
Codex is solid. I'm doing Godot development with Codex and GitHub Copilot and as long as you make sure to define the scope of the project as markdown files. Ask the AI to make dev logs in a local folder to the project (just use a .gdignore file so Godot doesn't get angry about the files) where it explains what feature it implemented, choices, what work still needs doing on the feature, and thoughts on the implementation. 

Start out by asking it to make a definition of best practices for the version of Godot you're using, for itself to follow as a local agent definition. Seriously helps. Make sure to put it on high effort for that part, and any major feature you need to implement.

comments.author: GenychDefake
comments.body:
Since GPT 5.5 is out, it's much much better code wise - it doesn't cover the code with a zillion fallbacks anymore.   
I would advice to not use MCPs. I tried Gopeak and Godot MCP – both are garbage, the others are less mature. Just ask Codex to write you compact cli for launching scenes, running tests and helpers for capturing debug output.

comments.author: fucklockjaw
comments.body:
Personally my experience has been abysmal.  
Agents do fine without an Mcp and can edit scenes no problem and they can get your game running lickity split but the code quality is so horrible with GdScript specifically.  

I actually finally gave up on a side project because I initially vibed it out in 3 days and when I eventually looked at the code I saw 1000s of lines per file. I saw UI state driving game logic. Just so much backwards ass code and I spent 2 weeks untangling it and now I've given up.  

You'll see Codex use int instead of your enum values. Using VSCode with Godot is a nightmare because the agent will run into issues where something isn't found (because the file is new and a gd.uid hasn't been created until you focus back on Godot editor) so it makes a work around that is disgusting. So you have to constantly refresh VScode and focus the Godot editor.  

Idk must be a skill issue but I'm giving Unity a try with codex today wish me luck.

replies.author: Heavy-Worldliness-27
replies.body: The thing is if you expect Codex to understand what you think about without ever telling it the precise specs and architecture it is bound to create massive monoliths that mixes everything, but the problem here isn't exactly Codex tbh

replies.author: fucklockjaw
replies.body:
That's fine but it still doesn't solve the other issues I constantly run into.

Such as \`someVariable: int = MyEnum.SomeValue\`. Why is it using an int?

Or when it wants to extend a class it just created you'll see  
\`\`\`  
extends "res://Path/To/New/Class.gd"  
\`\`\`

or when it needs to access an @ export variable. This one really isn't "the worst" but you get this everywhere. Null checks as far as the eye can see.  
\`\`\`  
func DoThing() -> void:  
if export\_var == null:  
return

... other logic ...  
\`\`\`

I'm spending so much time fighting the system it drives me crazy.  
I bet it would do much better if I were using C# but I really like to post my stuff to Itch so having browser export is really important to me.
